Any finite relational candidate must supply a limit construction whose pure-state space is a compact homogeneous space under a connected group, and tomographic locality, before continuous-reversibility reconstructions of quantum theory apply. The limit is not canonical: the cyclic groups Z_n have a direct-limit closure U(1), which is connected, and an inverse limit, the profinite integers, which is totally disconnected. Paper G7 restricts the form of the limit: a finite subset of the Bloch sphere that is homogeneous leaves a cap of angular radius arccos(59/60) = 10.475 degrees uncovered, 14.835 degrees for orbits of rotation groups (G7-01-07), and by the theorems of Turing and Gelander no quantum pure-state space is a Gromov-Hausdorff limit of finite homogeneous metric spaces (G7-01-09). Finite stages therefore cannot have a transitive symmetry group; inhomogeneous approximants, finite generating data with unbounded words, and cyclic-group-valued phases remain. Edition Z2: for the second and third forms paper G8 gives a construction conditional on stated assumptions (events of unbounded walk length on a finite gain graph give, under a growth condition, a dense inhomogeneous subset of a complex or real projective space; G8-01-05); Directors A and B record inhomogeneous nets of an imported geometry. For the ray and the connection averaged over the quasi-momentum distribution of the packet the residual is 0.0735, 0.0273, 0.0135, 0.0071, 0.0029, 0.0016 site (exponent -1.1). Relation between walk lengths and order of the rule. Consistency of the pair measure under continuation is a requirement that a generic gain graph violates (Directors A, B; G9-01-01); a reason for it, or an alternative relation between the measures at different lengths, is not given. An additive weighting of returning walks by a class function of their holonomy is switching invariant (G8-01-01); a reason for excluding it, if the second-order rule is intended, is not given. Edition Z4: a conditional reason is given. A family of measures is one function on sets of histories exactly when it is consistent under continuation (G10-01-01), and then an additive invariant rule is a multiple of the count (G10-01-02): the first-order weighting of returning walks is not a function of sets of histories. That events are sets of histories is an assumption about the event structure and is not derived. Edition Z13: G10 Lemma 3.1 now carries its hypotheses in the statement: every vertex has an outgoing arc, and events and histories are those from one fixed starting vertex. Without the first, the identification of events with sets of histories fails at dead ends.
state: conditional reason given; the event structure is supplied

statement: Force and gain order. Decide whether gains of bounded order (in particular the orders 2, 3, 4, 6 for which the pair measure is independent of the character) can produce the rays of a weak force in a controlled limit, by some encoding other than the staircase tried in G9 Section 6.2, or prove that they cannot. Related: the long-time behaviour under a linear gain depends on the arithmetic of the field (Cedzich et al. 2013). Edition Z4: narrowed. An exact translation of the quasi-momentum needs the linear gain, hence gains of order at least 2 pi / Phi (G10-01-05). For gains of order q >= 3 wound through blocks no quasi-energy lies in the local spectrum of every block, except four band edges for q = 4 (G10-01-06). Instances: staircases of order 3, 4, 6 hold a walk within about one block for block lengths 16 and 64 up to 2048 steps, leak for block length 4 and spread ballistically for block length 1 (Cedzich et al.); an order-4 staircase reaches 0.69, 0.54, 0.16 of the mean-field displacement at block lengths 16, 64, 256. Open: a theorem on the dynamics; arrangements other than staircases (one quasi-periodic rounding was run and stayed within seven sites). Edition Z9: Director G's two-ray limit uses the field pi/M with the sheet order M = pi/(F delta^4) growing, as the exact translation of G10-01-05 requires; it does not concern gains of bounded order. Cost of the sheet plane it assumes, for the five-sheet word extended to M sheets (Director Z): about 0.202 M^2 records for residual 0.01 with joint probability near 2^(-s); for every instrument that leaves the sheets unread the probability is at most 2/(M(1 - eta)). Open: a native word near that bound.
state: unresolved; narrowed by two propositions; five adverse instances

statement: Admitted tests. The cubic Veronese model (Director G) has the qubit table on a designated family of pure tests; with those tests only it is the qubit, with all affine effects it is a different theory in which pure states at Bloch angle 60 degrees are perfectly distinguishable. A candidate has to state which tests are admitted and why, before a pure-state transition geometry can be attributed to it; a derivation of tomographic completeness of the designated tests is not given.

Event structure and carrier. Independent verification of the proofs of paper G10. A reason for taking events to be sets of histories. A classification of the rules consistent under continuation that are not sums over end vertices of a function of one modulus. A principle that selects a carrier on which a rule depending on the gains is consistent: with trivial gains the count is consistent on every digraph of constant out-degree, and the requirement that the transport be visible to the measure is a proposal without warrant. The statement of Li and So on isometries of l_p, cited from secondary sources, is to be inspected. Edition Z5: within the record-sum form the carrier is no longer restricted to the line: every connected signed carrier of degree two forces the square (G10-01-07). Open in addition: a proof for gains that are not real, and for degrees above two. Edition Z6: gains that are not real are covered for cyclic gains under the growth hypothesis (G10-01-09). Open in addition: whether a combination of conjugate rules with unequal weights is excluded by positivity or by composition; carriers on which the growth hypothesis fails; degrees above two. Edition Z7: positivity restricts the weights of the conjugate rules to a cone and composition selects one character (G10-01-10). A carrier without merging walks (the countable binary tree, Director G) makes every rule of the record-sum form the count, so merging is necessary for Theorem 5.2 and for the summary of Section 5. Open: carriers on which the growth hypothesis fails; degrees above two. Edition Z8: with the pairs of a vertex and a sheet as records, the form of the rule is the record-sum form on the signed lift and the rule is unique for every order (G10-01-11); the dependence of the classification on what counts as a record is thereby explicit. Open as before: carriers on which the growth hypothesis fails; degrees above two; rules outside the record-sum form. Edition Z9: one class outside the record-sum form is now classified, the pair rules with a kernel (G10-01-12); there the pair form, hence the second order, is assumed. Open as before: carriers on which the hypotheses on blocks fail (12 of 40 random carriers in the follow-up computation, each with a larger space of consistent kernels); degrees above two; rules that are neither pair rules nor of the record-sum form. Edition Z10: for pair rules the classification is complete for every degree and every finite abelian gain group under the hypothesis on quotients (G10-01-12). Open: rules of the record-sum form in degrees above two; carriers on which the hypothesis fails; non-abelian gain groups; rules that are neither pair rules nor of the record-sum form; infinite vertex sets were not examined by the challenger. Edition Z11: rules of the record-sum form in degrees above two: settled for two block types (degree three with gains of order 3 or 6; degree four with gains of order 4), where the rule is the square (G10-01-14). Open: other blocks, other degrees, higher orders (where the conjugate characters will enter), and the items of edition Z10. Edition Z12: rules of the record-sum form are classified for Fourier blocks of every degree (G10-01-15). Open: blocks of other forms (real Hadamard blocks with other sign patterns, blocks from non-cyclic groups), carriers without disjoint successor sets (where the square itself need not be consistent), countable carriers, and the items of edition Z10. Edition Z14: the classification of rules of the record-sum form no longer depends on the form of the blocks (G10-01-17). Dependence on the modulus cannot be weakened to invariance under units, signs and conjugation (Re(a^4) on the Gaussian integers). Open: carriers on which the abundance of gains fails, and whether it follows from finiteness and connectedness; characters of infinite order; a bound on the order K of the differences in the proof; rules that are neither pair rules nor of the record-sum form; non-abelian gain groups. Edition Z15: the abundance of gains is decided by the carrier: on a finite carrier with A*A = d, d >= 2, and strongly connected derived digraph, the gains at a vertex at one length form a coset of a subgroup of index r/r_0, and the consistent rules of the record-sum form are the conjugate squared moduli for the order of that subgroup (G10-01-18, G10-01-19). So for finite carriers with gains in the roots of unity and a merging pair the classification of record-sum rules is complete. Open: countable carriers; characters of infinite order; non-abelian gain groups; rules that are neither pair rules nor of the record-sum form. Edition Z16: the form of the rule is reduced, on carriers with full blocks, to a sum over end vertices of a function of the summed gains (G10-01-21). Two-input events do not suffice in degree three (a cubic survives for the Fourier block); all inputs of a block are needed. Open: carriers with a merging pair but no full block, for functions that are not of the modulus; the items of edition Z15. Edition Z17: the addition of gains at a common end vertex is no longer assumed on those carriers; it follows, through some character, for every part of the rule that is not the count (G10-01-24). Still assumed: the rule is a sum over end vertices and sees the walks at a vertex only through the multiset of their gains. Open: non-cyclic groups; rules that see more of a walk than its gain; rules that are not sums over end vertices; which of the forms L + Q are consistent on a whole carrier when the entries do not generate the group. Edition Z19: the multiset theorem holds for every finite abelian group of gains (G10-01-22 to G10-01-24 restated), so carriers whose gain group has no faithful character are covered; for groups that are not abelian the solutions are still an additive part plus a quadratic form (G10 Remark 5.21), with a description of the forms by irreducible representations that is conditional. Open as before: rules that see more of a walk than its gain; rules that are not sums over end vertices; which forms L + Q are consistent on a whole carrier when the entries do not generate the group; the non-abelian forms beyond two computed groups. Edition Z20: the same function at every end vertex, a full block and generating block entries are no longer assumed on strongly connected carriers with abundant gains (G10-01-26). Still assumed: additivity over events with disjoint sets of end vertices; dependence on a walk through its gain alone; the value zero on the empty multiset; the carrier. Open: parallel arcs with merging, unequal out-degrees, non-abelian groups, carriers that are not strongly connected (a closed form for the quadratic part), and everything that selects between the count and the squares. Edition Z21: the classification of edition Z20 needed every gain at every vertex at one length, which fails on periodic carriers such as the even rings. It now holds, for the values of the rule on events, on every finite carrier of constant out-degree without parallel arcs whose derived digraph is strongly connected (G10-01-28 to G10-01-30); characters with equal or inverse restrictions to the subgroup of quotients of gains that meet at one vertex at one length give the same rule. Open as before, and: carriers whose derived digraph is not strongly connected. Edition Z22: a consistent rule of this kind that is multiplicative on product events of the carrier with itself at large lengths is zero, the count, or the squared norm for one class of characters (G10-01-31): mixtures of the count with a square are excluded and the normalization is fixed. What selects between the count and a square, and among the characters, is open. Edition Z23: with near-return as a premise the count is excluded (G10-01-32), and with multiplicativity the rule is the squared norm for one class of characters (G10-01-31). Open: a derivation of near-return, or of reversibility of the complete system, from the carrier; the choice among the characters. Edition Z24: correction to the entry of the previous edition: near-return is not a premise about the system. Open: a derivation, from the carrier, of any one frequency fact equivalent to a = 0; why the record at a vertex is the gain and nothing finer (with the last arc recorded, no consistent rule of this form exists); the choice among the characters. Edition Z25: the demand of consistency on every event is removed on the signed line and rings (G10-01-33 to G10-01-35).
